data.author: Fleur Hargreaves

A growing number of Democratic lawmakers are ramping up pressure on Israel, introducing legislation to impose sanctions on illegal Israeli settlements in the West Bank and Gaza.
The Stop the Settlements Act, led by Representatives Joaquin Castro, Madeleine Dean, Don Beyer, Greg Casar, Sara Jacobs and Veronica Escobar, would block new settlement construction or expansion through sanctions and a ban on importing goods made in settlements and outposts.

Israel turned Gaza into 'largest and harshest ghetto' in modern history, Euro-Med says
Euro-Med Human Rights Monitor said that Israel has turned Gaza into the "largest and harshest ghetto" in modern history.
The human rights organisation pointed to Israel's use of starvation “as a lethal weapon", the enclave's diminishing health care system, as well as severe shortages of necessary equipment, aid and other humanitarian needs.
"The consequences of turning Gaza into a ghetto extend beyond the constant threat of death, striking at the heart of its economic and social structure," the rights group said.
"Entire families have become wholly dependent on aid to survive after losing their homes and income, with no prospect of restoring their normal lives."
The Euro-med press release comes amid Israel's continued and deliberate concentration of over two million people in less than 30 percent of the Gaza Strip. The enclave is considered to have the highest population density in the world.

data.title: Middle East Eye: What missiles and drones do the Houthis have?
data.author: Mera Aladam
data.summary:
What missiles and drones do the Houthis have?
A rapid offensive by Yemen’s Houthis has intensified the country’s civil war and caused chaos in global oil markets.
The group, which has controlled much of northern Yemen for over a decade, has seized fresh territory from the pro-government forces and threatened shipping traffic, notably that of Saudi Arabia, in the Bab el-Mandeb strait, the maritime chokepoint linking the Gulf of Aden to the Red Sea and the Suez Canal.
With few signs of military formality, the group has often been described in international media as a "ragtag fighting force".
But over the past two decades, the Houthis have evolved to use missiles and drones to stage attacks inside Yemen as well as against Israel, Saudi Arabia and the UAE, among others.
Much of the group’s arsenal has either been designed or supplied by Iran, which regards the force as a member of its Axis of Resistance, a network of allies that also includes Hamas and Hezbollah.
The Houthis have also acquired weapons, including decades-old Soviet-era tanks and helicopters, after victory on the battlefield, and recently seized US-supplied military vehicles captured from retreating Saudi-backed forces.
While the Houthis’ stockpile levels are unknown, it is possible to assemble a sense of their firepower and military capabilities.
